tasks.title: Media inspection service

tasks.title: Auth integration decision
tasks.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam that the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range

tasks.title: Profile model
tasks.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

tasks.title: Progress persistence
tasks.acceptance: Progress rows are scoped to a profile id rather than a user id and keyed by (profileId, contentId) so a repeated write upserts idempotently, with read and write authorized against the active profile; two devices writing the same title are resolved by a server-issued writer epoch rather than by client timestamps or by a monotonically-increasing-position rule, because client clocks are unreliable and a monotonic rule wrongly refuses a legitimate rewind; and writes go directly to PostgreSQL, with no Redis write-behind introduced until a PostgreSQL problem has actually been measured

tasks.title: Watchlist persistence
tasks.acceptance: Typed add, remove, and list APIs with authorization

tasks.title: Playback session API
tasks.acceptance: Server resolves authorized provider candidates and clients cannot submit arbitrary media URLs; the session response is a discriminated union on outcome (granted, denied, unavailable) with reasons present on every branch rather than as an optional field, because a denial with no reason trail violates the reason-trail invariant exactly as much as a grant with none

tasks.title: Player state machine
tasks.acceptance: The machine models the session and candidate lifecycle (resolving, loading a candidate, playing, buffering, seeking, recovering, failing over, ended, fatal) rather than UI state, which the controls layer already owns; the video element and the playback engine stay authoritative and the machine is a validated projection of them, so every engine and media event has an inbound transition even in states where it supposedly cannot occur

tasks.title: Search loses text typed before hydration
tasks.acceptance: Text typed into the search field before the form hydrates is not lost: on mount the form adopts the DOM value if it differs from its own state, and a query typed at any point becomes an addressable URL. Proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run on WebKit, where the race reproduces, rather than only on Chromium where it does not. Separately the spec addresses the result heading exactly rather than by substring, because role-name matching is substring by default and a query equal to a title matches both the results heading and the card heading -- a spec defect that only appeared once the suite was first executed.

tasks.title: notFound() never reaches the wire: dead addresses answer 200
tasks.acceptance: An unknown title id and a malformed watch id each answer HTTP 404 rather than a skeleton served at 200, proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run rather than by a route calling notFound(). The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. Any fix must keep the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. DEPENDS ON PL-0103 because the title route is that task's declared write surface and it is currently in REVIEW; this is a lifecycle dependency, not a technical one.

tasks.title: Review dependency scope and provenance reconciliation
tasks.acceptance: SCOPE EXPANDED, deliberately and on the reviewer's ruling: this task now covers two trust-boundary features in the same two files, because the review system binds an approval to a path range rather than to a semantic hunk, so a current-head review of these files cannot truthfully exclude the second. A nominal second task over the identical write surface was rejected as a fake logical split. (1) allowedPaths remains the sole write, collision and staging surface while review fingerprints, stale-review checks, approvals and the DONE gate bind to allowedPaths union reviewDependencies; two tasks with disjoint allowedPaths and a shared reviewDependency can be active simultaneously, and editing that shared dependency invalidates both reviews; tasks without reviewDependencies behave identically to before; a declaration that reduces to the repository root is refused rather than dropped, in validation and at point of use, and the autonomy guard treats root ownership as orchestration. (2) Provenance reconciliation: an implementation already present in COMMITTED GIT HISTORY can be started with a true implementationBaseSha via explicit flags that are refused on an ordinary start, the base is validated against mechanical facts only, the semantic question of whether it is really this implementation's predecessor is published as evidence for the reviewer rather than guessed at by a heuristic, and the audit event is distinguishable from an ordinary start. The contract says committed rather than pushed deliberately: the mechanism inspects the local worktree and the local graph and consults no remote, so a clean branch of never-pushed commits satisfies it, and claiming otherwise was the same class of provenance overclaim this task exists to remove.
